main_text.head: CAP. VII.

head.i: Tertium nostrum Argumentum contra Meritum de Condigno, ex Confessionibus Pontificiorum locupletissimis, ex parte Dignationis Dei remunerantis[?].

main_text.head: SECT. I.
main_text.p: N[?]Vllum opus, quod præmium æternæ vitæ obtinet ex bonita-te & dignatione Dei remunerantis, potest dici Meritorium de Condigno apud Deum:
At omne opus bonum præmium æternæ vitæ obtinet ex benignitate & dignatione Dei:
Propterea nullum opus bonum est Meritorium de condigno apud Deum.

Majorem Vasquez clarè profitetur in Di-ctatoria Censura sua de Protestantium doctri-na:Vasquez in 1.2.Tom 2.disp.214. Cap. 5. n. 23. § Quod vero. {o}Operibus bonis (inquit) secundum se dignitatem vita æterna negant, sed referunt eorum dignitatem in favorem Dei, & acceptationem per Christi merita: quod nihil aliud est, quàm veram & perfectam rationem Meriti operibus nostris denegare. Sic ille, & quidem verissimè: quia nullum Meritum quod opus habet Dei acceptatione, potest dici in Condigni-tate operantis consistere secundum Æquali-

page.notes: The left edge of the scan shows part of the neighbouring page (page 62 or the facing page) with its own text and notes; not transcribed, as it is not on this printed page. The page number reads "63"; the digits are blurred, so this is a reading to check. The running head at the top is faint and I could not read it reliably; left as illegible. The decorated initial is read as N (joined to "Vllum"); its letter is uncertain, hence [?]. "remunerantis" in the italic title line is a doubtful reading (possibly "remunerantis" or "remuneratis"), marked [?]. The reference mark in the text is a small circle "o", matched to the marginal note. The catchword "tatem" sits at the right below the last line; the text ends with the last full line "Æquali-". The signature "I" is centred below the text block.
